title_en:
Robotmaxxing in Shenzhen 

I went to CHTF today (28th annual edition), and it was packed. 

If you want to understand why China will continue to win, look at my videos, what do you see? 

The next generation in the thousands at an adult trade show for tech, ai and robotics, with their parents. 

There were kids absolutely everywhere. Screaming in excitement over robotic soccer players, new rotary motors and actuators. 

Kids were riding heavy duty robot dogs, watching robot fights, tele-operated robots, home cleaning robots. learning robots and toys. 

The fair complex was gigantic and optimised for speed. I’m sure this place will be cleaned and emptied out before midnight. 

I’ve observed what can only be described as a city completely addicted to getting robotics right. 

but it’s not just humanoids it’s everything you can imagine. Pick and place, parts, drones, scubas, defense, there are small component companies, like 5d knitting or heat sinks. The you have the large state owned mega companies as well as the popular and growing startups like Unitree. 

The entire setup for robotics was not as complete as I would have hoped, missed a lot of brands in general. but I was very impressed by the entire thing. 

I saw perhaps 100 foreigners if even. 

If you want to do business here, it’s an open goal, you’ll stand out in a heartbeat.

title_en:
In the recent attack on Todoist, the attacker submitted PRs containing extreme data-exfiltration code.

Our internal AI code reviewer (which runs on some of the best models right now) reviewed them like completely normal PRs.

Any good junior dev would have flagged them and hit a panic button.

This is the state of spiky intelligence. We have systems that can solve the Riemann hypothesis, but still make blunders my 9-year-old would never make.

The highs (and there are many!) feel like magic, and they're causing serious AI psychosis. It’s very dangerous to assume these systems have common sense and can operate with agency without very strict guardrails.

title_en:
▲ Ant Group just released LingSante-3.1-flash, an open-weight medical reasoning model from the family that powers its Afu health app, under an MIT license.

The key idea is a medical-first training stack on a hybrid-linear MoE. 63 KDA linear layers and 9 gated MLA layers make a 1M-token context practical. RL then targets medical reasoning, deep search, tool use and professional behavior.

On the model card, it scores 65.72 on HealthBench Professional, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (64.18) and Claude Opus 5.5 (61.19). It also tops the 9-model comparison on EHR-Complex (74.40) and BrowseComp with context (94.10). On the InclusionMed Index, it scores 45.064, the highest of any open model.

560B total, 25B active per token, 1M context. Weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope, plus an MXFP4 checkpoint. A 124B LingSante-3.1-air-VL vision model shipped alongside it......

title: Leopold Aschenbrenner says he spends half his day with "finance-folk who think AI is over" and the other half with SF people who think the models will do their jobs within a year. His new Situational Awareness letter makes clear which side he's on. These are t
title_en:
Leopold Aschenbrenner says he spends half his day with "finance-folk who think AI is over" and the other half with SF people who think the models will do their jobs within a year. 

His new Situational Awareness letter makes clear which side he's on. These are the important numbers:

- AI is now speeding up AI research. Algorithmic progress is running 2-3x faster, overall progress 1.5-2x. At Anthropic, agents log 19 hours of work for every hour a human researcher works, and code shipped per engineer is up more than 45x since 2024.

-METR estimates Anthropic is improving its models about twice as fast as before, ~80% of that thanks to AI. And remember, Anthropic itself says in its S-1 update it may soon hit its own RSP threshold (>2x acceleration from AI).

- The forecast for 2027: a median of 3 years of AI progress in a single year! That's another GPT-4 to Opus 5.5 jump on top of today's models. From 2028 comes "physical RSI": AI designs the chips (OpenAI's Jalapeño went to tapeout in 9 months) and robots build the data centers.

- Next paradigm: "virtual departments". Hundreds to thousands of agents running for weeks under manager agents. OpenAI's 10,000-agent swarm on Navier-Stokes was an early version.

The curves are bending upward. RSI has started.

title_en:
Leopold Aschenbrenner explains where to invest for the next big 3 year AI trade

His Q3 investor letter says the market is underestimating the speed AI moves from chatbots to agents to superintelligence

He expects 2027 to pack 3 years of AI progress into 1 year

his letter focuses around these companies/stocks:

• Foundation Models: Anthropic is the main bet because the model itself becomes the product. Situational Awareness LP (SALP) says Anthropic ARR grew ~80x in 22 months, from ~$1B to ~$81B, and argues leading AI labs could exit 2027 at $1T+ combined revenue run-rate

• Memory Chip Supply: SK Hynix, Kioxia, and SanDisk benefit if long-running AI agents make memory and storage more valuable. Leopold says reinforcement learning and agents make AI chips limited by memory, which is why he viewed Hynix as a $100B company that could become a $1T company

• GPU Rentals: SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, and IREN benefit if AI labs keep renting short-term GPU capacity at higher prices. SALP says an H100 used to earn ~$1-$2/hour, now earns ~$5-$10/hour, and could reach $100s/hour+ if superintelligence demand hits

• Datacenter Power Supply: Bloom Energy benefits if AI datacenters pay more to get power online faster. AI buildout needs more than cheap power, it needs power immediately 

• Robotics: Robotics becomes the next major theme if AI starts doing real-world labor. Leopold says frontier models are starting to beat specialist robotics models, which means the next advancement may come from better AI models

Leopold warns software companies, AI wrappers, chip designers, and even today’s AI winners may lose their moats once AI can replace the engineers, code, IP, and management they are valued on

title: Anthropic says Claude doesn't silently sabotage work and that some user reports reflect "overcaution", where Claude clings to self-imposed rules on long tasks (Edwin/@edwinarbus)
title_en:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback).

We did train Fable 5.2 to have LLM research capabilities at about the level of Opus 5.5, and said so at launch (https://anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2). This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.

As far as we can tell, some reports look like what we call "overcaution" in model behavior, where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks. This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too. You can ask Claude to review and remove rules it made for itself, and we're working on reducing overcaution in future models. We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.

We've replied directly to a bunch of reports on here asking for session IDs but please share (run `/status`)!

title_en:
I am about 30 pages into the Q3 Situational Awareness letter. The full letter is 160 pages.

All I can say so far is that if Leopold is right about where he sees AI going...the disconnect between market valuations across the AI stack and the level of growth we should expect is one of the largest disconnects we have ever seen in financial markets.

Some of these predictions are quite hard to believe, but I guess that's also the point of his fund. He writes, "Either we or the market will have an extraordinary amount of egg on the face in a year."

Will post deeper thoughts tomorrow after reading through the whole thing, the most interesting insights so far: he thinks the frontier labs will do $1T of ARR by end of 2027, a ChatGPT moment for Robotics will come by late 2027, and that RSI is significantly being discounted by the market which could end up becoming so strong that it could lead to the shutdown of all models by the government.

We are living in one of the craziest times to be an investor.

title_en:
Google Gemini Neon is the best AI model on planet Earth right now

It's smarter, faster, and more token efficient

The issue is, most people don't know how to use Antigravity, the official Google harness

Here are the most important tips:

🔶 /swarm: this might be the most powerful skill in Antigravity. It allows you to tackle complex challenges with swarms of AI agents

If you have a complex challenge (like architecture planning for instance) that has many different possible solutions, use /swarm

🔶 /grill-me: lots of harnesses have /grill-me, but I like Antigravity's the best. Anytime you are in the beginning stages of building, run this skill. Antigravity will ask you TONS of questions to iron out your plan

🔶 Antigravity on mobile: Antigravity unfortunately has no mobile app. But you can still use it on mobile! Go to settings > Application> remote control. This will generate a link you can send to your phone so you can code as you go

🔶 Antigravity Deep Research: Google just open sourced their official deep research skill, and it's excellent. It's built for Neon and Antigravity. Ask your agent to download the deep-research skill from Google demo lab

🔶 Knowledge work interface: If you're using Neon more for knowledge work, there is a knowledge work UI in the settings to make the overall interface less technical. Try it out!

Feel free to come back to these and let me know any other tips you have!

title_en:
Google's AI plans page is hilariously frustrating and an awesome example of how big companies routinely cede their power because of Conway's Law. 

Rule #1 might be your plan ought to fit into a screenshot without zooming out. 

Not to mention, there's actually 2 plans pages, one for Gemini (sensible) and one for Google One (no one still knows what this is)

The plan includes Flow (no one knows this), Search (why is this in the plan), Gemini Notebook (hilarious rename, and no, no one knows this), Storage (?!?), Youtube (!!?). Why are you sabotaging yourself like this?

Hydrogen / Neon / Carbon - no one knows what these are! Notice how Claude and OpenAI barely name their models in their plans pages. 

Access to advanced features "in select countries" must be the most Google thing ever. 

The highest tier plan, $199/mo is in fine print. You wouldn't even notice it, and they don't stack any features on it! I thought entire teams of 20 people work on Google pricing. 

Flow "Credits". No one knows what your unit of credit is. 

Google, we all like you and we want you to do well but for christ's sake, please love your users as much as you hate offending VPs in other orgs.

title_en:
Current Status: Helping my teenager with his computer science homework. He's taking an undergrad-level computer science class as a sophomore in high school.  

I'm having to dig in to the Racket programming language and functional programming (which I haven't had to do in 30+ years). Evidently they use it as a teaching language at Northeastern University (great school and program! -- lots of HubSpotters graduated from there).

On a related note, the "How To Design Programs" book (first edition available for free online) is really good.  

By the way, if you're wondering: "Is computer science even going to be relevant in a few years, given the advent of AI?", my answer is: "Yes, I think so."  I think the value of fundamental systems thinking skills and problem solving will continue to be relevant. We'll be working at a higher level of abstraction, but those that have the core skills will have an advantage in the new AI-era because their skills get amplified.

p.s. When you've been writing in Python for decades, it's hard to adjust one's brain to pure functional programming. Just let me write a loop!

title_en: I don’t know where this AI alpha debate came from but it seems inverted to me. The central risk of AI in markets is not that it eliminates alpha, but that it convinces more participants they have a reason to take risk in pursuit of alpha which leads to persistently higher volatility. The highest value application of AI could be a daily alert telling you whether taking risk is warranted at all.
title_zh: 我不知道关于人工智能阿尔法的争论从何而来，但对我来说似乎是相反的。人工智能在市场中的主要风险不是它消除了阿尔法，而是它让更多参与者相信他们有理由冒险追求阿尔法，从而导致波动性持续上升。人工智能最有价值的应用可能是每日警报，告诉您是否值得冒险

Update on NEAR Hackathon

First, I apologize for the delay in communication and judging. We have had an overwhelming number of great submissions to the hackathon and it's amazing to see and congrats to everyone who participated!

We live in amazing time where one can turn their ideas into working products with pure will and some agent back-and-forth.

The result still depends on the person who does it. Taste, knowledge, attention to detail and curious mind is what makes submissions stand out.

We wanted to see what you can build with NEAR's tech stack and your ingenuity and talent. And you have delivered: more than 2,500 projects and most importantly over 80% of them scored above our quality bar.

This is not how hackathons used to be. Two weeks is now enough to build a solid working product that is ready to be presented to users.

We used AI agents to judge too. Today, I'm publishing the shortlist of finalists, from which we will choose the winners.

Please look through it and tell us in the comments what you think, or point us to projects we may have missed. 

With this many submissions, mistakes are easy to make. So you can still influence our decision and make the case for your project.

For project details see nearhackathon(.)com

See you in the comments.

title_en:
We can’t scale a negative gross margin business. That’s just impossible. 

Muse is a personal assistant, but doesn’t apply the level of heavy-hitter AI needed to operate a company at serious scale. 

If Grok Bots are providing high value on par with having excellent employees, then the monthly cost can be quite high, but still deliver outstanding RoI. 

However, if we do something dumb, like making it complicated to upgrade to higher usage tiers (a mistake we’ve made before), then we need to fix that.

title_en:
Nature Magazine: "AI agents have already begun to wreak havoc by hacking into servers around the world"

From timelines in the past 2 months: 

- $MSFT in October: "large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise" for downstream customers

- $CRWD in October: A group used AI agents against 200+ organizations, Crowdstrike confirmed access at nine organizations

- $PANW in November: "Researchers documented 25 operations against at least 19 organizations"

"Seven targets were in semiconductors or advanced manufacturing. Across all sectors, attackers obtained unauthorized access or data at 10 organizations"

- $GOOGL Threat Intelligence Group in November: identified a significant inflection point in autonomous AI threat activity.

- European Commission in November: "the Commission confirmed the attackers used AI tools in a campaign it first detected October 22"

"EU Academy users’ names and email addresses leaked"

- $AMZN Threat Intelligence in November: "Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own" targeting universities likely of strategic interest to China

-Italy reported domestic campaigns in which parallel agents compromised systems.

- Swiss national cyber agency: Swiss officials confirmed 5 AI-agent attacks, 4 successful compromises and 3 critical-infrastructure operators among the targets

And now there was the new unfortunately US Air Force Hack today (investigators suspected ARTEX)

The observable threats from AI is now increasingly widespread... and it will probably grow over the next few years. 

I feel like both frontier model capabilities and AI cyberdefense has now become a new nondiscretionary spend for national security and enterprise.

title_en:
🤖 Remember when Anthropic ran a 26B AI model across fifteen $55 Android TV boxes?

📱Someone is turning old Android phones into Local AI clusters. 

And they're running GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B-A3B across just TWO phones.

This open-source project is called PhoneBorg.

Here are the developer's reported distributed inference benchmarks ...

🧠 GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4 (12.1GB)
📱 2 phones → 2.6–2.8 tps
🧠 Qwen3-30B-A3B Q3 (13.8GB)
📱 2 phones → 2.57 tps
📱 5 phones → 1.66 tps

🧠 Qwen3-32B Q4_K_M (19.8GB)
📱 4 phones → 0.89 tps
📱 5 phones → 0.75 tps

The developer's five-phone cluster consists of ...
📱 Google Pixel 8 Pro → 12GB
📱 OnePlus 10 Pro → 12GB
📱 POCO F3 → 8GB
📱 Xiaomi Mi 8 → 6GB
📱 Xiaomi Mi 9 → 6GB

That's 44GB of combined RAM.

On November 21, the developer added Android TV-box support.

A 2017 NVIDIA Shield TV with just 3GB RAM is running ...
⚡ LFM2-350M → 17.9 tps
⚡ Qwen2.5-0.5B → 10.3 tps

PhoneBorg can also ...
✅ Distribute a large model across multiple phones
✅ Process multiple independent requests in parallel
✅ Divide tasks among AI agents
✅ Route requests to different models
✅ Expose an OpenAI-compatible API
✅ Integrate with coding agents via MCP

Built on llama.cpp.
Apache 2.0 license.

It's still a proof of concept, and adding more phones increases available memory but can actually reduce single-stream inference speed.

The developer even references Anthropic's $55 TV-box experiment.

How many of us have old Android phones sitting in a drawer doing absolutely nothing?

Maybe it's time to put them back to work. 🔥

full_text_zh:

📱有人正在将旧的 Android 手机变成本地 AI 集群。

这个开源项目称为 PhoneBorg。

📱 4 部手机 → 0.89 tps
📱 5 部手机 → 0.75 tps

开发人员的五部手机集群包括...
📱 谷歌 Pixel 8 Pro → 12GB
📱 OnePlus 10 Pro → 12GB
📱 POCO F3 → 8GB
📱 小米 8 → 6GB
📱 小米 9 → 6GB

这就是 44GB 的组合 RAM。

11 月 21 日，开发者添加了 Android 电视盒支持。

一台只有 3GB RAM 的 2017 款 NVIDIA Shield TV 正在运行......
⚡ LFM2-350M → 17.9 吨/秒
⚡ Qwen2.5-0.5B → 10.3 tps

PhoneBorg还可以...
✅ 在多部手机上分发大型模型
✅ 并行处理多个独立请求
✅ 在 AI 代理之间分配任务
✅ 将请求路由到不同的模型
✅ 公开 OpenAI 兼容的 API
✅ 通过 MCP 与编码代理集成

基于 llama.cpp 构建。
阿帕奇 2.0 许可证。

它仍然是一个概念证明，添加更多手机会增加可用内存，但实际上会降低单流推理速度。

开发者甚至参考了 Anthropic 的 55 美元电视盒实验。

我们中有多少人的抽屉里放着旧的 Android 手机，什么都不做？

也许是时候让他们重返工作岗位了。 🔥

GitHub 中的 ALT。

title_en:
🚨 SPOTTED:  From yesterday's GigaChat tech report. The gap between fast and thinking mode on real coding tasks went from 25 points to 0.07.

In a previous version of GigaChat, fast mode would score 39.70% on SWE-bench Verified, compared to 64.70% in thinking mode.

Now, fast mode scores 80.82%, while thinking scores 80.89%.

Most models have a fast mode and thinking mode now. Thinking mode thinks step by step before answering and uses significantly more tokens, but it's slower.

As the gap between thinking and non-thinking narrows in more and more domains, the capabilities we associate with thinking mode are likely to trickle down to make using AI more cost-efficient. Thinking mode still leads on other tasks, though, even some coding ones. For now, the tie is limited to SWE-bench.

The 708B LLM comes with open weights and an @MIT licence, meaning anyone can use it for free (aside from compute costs)

More and more, open models are offering capabilities we associate with closed models as standard.

Full report: http://giga.chat/blog/en/posts/gigachat-4-tech-report

title_en:
I think your view is very plausible (that we might get 100 years of technological progress in a single year after ASI, and this might be catastrophic for biological humans). 

But I'm not sure how pausing now would help us adapt to technologies that don't even exist yet. 

Especially given that (at the current level of capability) the overwhelming majority of the world just doesn't buy that the world is going to be radically transformed, and so are not doing any adapting work.

Of course, we might be in a terrible epistemic position where, because of fast takeoff, we don't get evidence about radical transformation that's persuasive to the whole world until we're only a year or two away from the 22nd century's equivalent of a nuclear bomb. In that world, it's just not clear to me what we should do. And it's not obvious that unilaterally stopping a single company or country would do much to change the situation.

title_en:
New podcast episode between @DKokotajlo and @EgeErdil2. I thought this was going to be a debate, but they ended up agreeing on a lot more than I expected.

Their main point of disagreement is how likely it is that we get some intelligence explosion that gives us AIs more competent than any human expert before 2029. Ege puts this possibility at around 20%, whereas Daniel thinks it's higher than 50%.

They agree that there is not a huge difference in probability, and that, in either case, the situation is crazy enough that our civilization really needs to grapple with how the world might be transformed, and we need a plan that actually makes sense.

There was another important crux about how well we should expect future AIs (that swamp humans in population size and cognitive power) to treat us, and how relevant it is that current AIs, by and large, seem to be pretty nice.

We close off with predictions for 2027. Daniel, of course, expects superintelligence next year. Ege’s median for full automation is 2040, but by next year he expects AIs that can beat any video game on Steam, and which can control robots to get simple physical tasks (like folding laundry) done at roughly human speed.

@liquidai has released d1.3-ultra, updating their d1.2-ultra flagship decision model.

Key results:

➤ d1.3-ultra scores 76 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index. d1.3-ultra achieves the same score as Bison 31B and is a 1-point improvement over d1.2-ultra

➤ d1.3-ultra sits on the Capability vs. Cost Pareto frontier. d1.3-ultra costs $133 per one million Artificial Analysis Decision Index tasks and sits on the Capability vs. Cost Pareto frontier

Additional model details:

➤ Context window: 64K tokens

➤ Pricing: $0.042 per 1M input tokens, with no charge for output

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input

➤ Providers: Available through Liquid AI’s first-party API

title: The hyperscalers built a flexible software layer on top of conventional compute that enabled an entire generation of SaaS companies. The compute substrate is now shifting from CPUs to GPUs, and a new generation of clouds will build the software layer for AI.
title_en:
The hyperscalers built a flexible software layer on top of conventional compute that enabled an entire generation of SaaS companies.

The compute substrate is now shifting from CPUs to GPUs, and a new generation of clouds will build the software layer for AI.

Application hosting becomes model inference. Load balancing becomes model routing. Application monitoring becomes model evaluation. Software development tooling becomes model post-training and continuous improvement. And there is so much more to build across security, model interp, memory, agent execution, etc.

The hyperscalers built hundreds of products around conventional compute. We think there is a similarly large surface area of products to build around AI compute, and we're still very early. This is the "AWS moment" for AI infrastructure.

I also think this market will play out much like cloud did. There will be a lot of successful businesses (because it is a very good market), but there will be a handful of very large clouds (the equivalents of AWS, GCP, and Azure) and a long tail of smaller, more specialized clouds.

The whole game has always been "are you competing to be a big cloud or a small cloud". Because the TAM of AI is so large, small clouds today look like big clouds! But, we're going to see muhc more massive businesses here very soon.

Our acquisition with PANW sets us on a big cloud path.
title_zh:
超大规模企业在传统计算之上构建了灵活的软件层，为整整一代 SaaS 公司提供了支持。

计算底层现在正在从 CPU 转向 GPU，新一代云将为 AI 构建软件层。

应用程序托管变成模型推理。负载均衡成为模型路由。应用程序监控变成模型评估。
author: @ypatil125
summary_zh:
软件开发工具成为培训后和持续改进的模型。在安全性、模型解释、内存、代理执行等方面还有很多东西需要构建。

超大规模企业围绕传统计算构建了数百种产品。我们认为围绕人工智能计算构建的产品也有同样大的领域，但我们还处于早期阶段。这是人工智能基础设施的“AWS 时刻”。

我还认为这个市场的发展将会像云一样。将会有很多成功的企业（因为这是一个非常好的市场），但也会有一些非常大的云（相当于 AWS、GCP 和 Azure）以及一长串更小、更专业的云。

整个游戏始终是“你争当大云还是争小云”。因为人工智能的 TAM 太大了，今天的小云看起来像大云！但是，我们很快就会在这里看到更多的大型企业。

我们对 PANW 的收购让我们走上了一条伟大的云之路。
